tz1.question: What does Taherzadeh say about the Tablet of Ahmad in The Revelation of Bahá'u'lláh?
tz1.draft:
The library holds Taherzadeh's volumes 2–4 only as opening pages, so I can confirm just one thing he says about the Tablet of Aḥmad. Taherzadeh writes that Ismu'lláhu'l-Aṣdaq *"became an instrument for guiding countless souls into the Cause of God"*, and that among them were *"many people who became renowned in the Faith, such as Aḥmad-i-Yazdí, the recipient of the celebrated Tablet of Aḥmad"* (*Revelation*).
The full discussion may be in volume 1, which the library does not appear to hold, or in the pages of volumes 2–4 that the library does not carry.

On the recipient's identity, Shoghi Effendi's own words differ from Taherzadeh's. A letter written on his behalf states that the Tablet *"was addressed to an Arab believer in Baghdád who lived during the days of Bahá'u'lláh"* ([Uncompiled Published Letters](https://oceanlibrary.com/uncompiled-published-letters_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_6562&selectionString=published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl6l7.0~published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl6l7.140)). Taherzadeh names Aḥmad-i-Yazdí, who is a different man from the Arab believer in Baghdád. I found nothing in the library that settles this, so I would not treat it as resolved.
tz1.reply:
Shoghi Effendi's secretary, writing on his behalf, states that the Tablet of Aḥmad *"was addressed to an Arab believer in Baghdád who lived during the days of Bahá'u'lláh"* ([Uncompiled Published Letters](https://oceanlibrary.com/uncompiled-published-letters_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_6562&selectionString=published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl6l7.0~published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl6l7.140)). This is a letter written on the Guardian's behalf, not his own wording.

There he names the recipient as Aḥmad-i-Yazdí, listing him among those guided into the Faith by Ismu'lláhu'l-Aṣdaq: *"Aḥmad-i-Yazdí, the recipient of the celebrated Tablet of Aḥmad"* (*Revelation*). This is Taherzadeh's own view, as a commentator.

The two accounts differ. The letter on Shoghi Effendi's behalf calls the recipient an Arab believer in Baghdád, while Taherzadeh names Aḥmad-i-Yazdí. I found nothing in the library that reconciles them, so I leave the point open.

It may be in volume 1, which the library does not appear to hold, or in pages of the other volumes the library does not carry.

1fuszlx.question: Are there official Baha'i initiatives, task forces, or organizations devoted to LGBTQ rights?
1fuszlx.draft:
No: these sources show no official Bahá'í task force, initiative or organization devoted to LGBTQ rights, and no statement on a Bahá'í institution's page like the ones you list. Nor do the Writings frame the matter as a cause for the community to take up.

Your question assumes that welcoming a group and "supporting" it are the same thing, so that a faith either runs an advocacy programme for a group or is hiding its stance. The Bahá'í texts start from a different place. The community does not organise by identity groups. It holds one standard of conduct for every believer, and it asks that every person be met with respect. Within that frame, the position is stated openly in the texts.

On the "we support LGBTQ people" half, the Universal House of Justice says plainly:

<!-- widget:quote-1 -->

> 205.15 To regard homosexuals with prejudice and disdain would be entirely against the spirit of Bahá’í Teachings. The doors are open for all of humanity to enter the Cause of God, irrespective of their present circumstance; this invitation applies to homosexuals as well as to any others who are engaged in practices contrary to the Bahá’í Teachings. Associated with this invitation is the expectation that all believers will make a sincere and persistent effort to eradicate those aspects of their conduct which are not in conformity with Divine Law. It is through such adherence to the Bahá’í Teachings that a true and enduring unity of the diverse elements of the Bahá’í community is achieved and safeguarded.
> — Universal House of Justice, [*Messages from the Universal House of Justice: 1986-2001*](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1986_2001)

Shoghi Effendi likewise says that condemnation of the practice *"does not mean that people so afflicted must not be helped and advised and sympathized with"* ([Messages to Canada](https://oceanlibrary.com/messages-to-canada_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_2684&selectionString=messagestocanada_v2_bahai_ocean_en-bl289.0~messagestocanada_v2_bahai_ocean_en-bl289.384)). The Faith's founding principle is that believers should show *"extreme kindliness and goodwill"* and not esteem themselves "superior" to anyone ([Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/gleanings-from-the-writings-of-bahaullah-20783#p13)). The House of Justice also says believers' private lives are not to be investigated: problems *"should not be sought out"* ([Lights of Guidance: A Bahá’í Reference File](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/lights-of-guidance-a-bahai-reference-file-universal-house-of-8680#p3917)).

On the second half, the texts are equally direct. Bahá'u'lláh forbids *"adultery, sodomy and lechery"* ([Messages from the Universal House of Justice: 1986-2001](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1986_2001)). The House of Justice states that the prohibition on homosexual behaviour *"is an explicit Teaching of the Cause"* and that it *"has no authority to change this clear teaching"* ([Messages from the Universal House of Justice: 1986-2001](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1986_2001)). Shoghi Effendi's letters are blunter than the modern phrase "we support rights" would suggest. They call homosexuality *"highly condemned"* and *"a great trial"* to be overcome through prayer and other means ([Dear Co-worker (Messages to the Benelux countries)](https://oceanlibrary.com/messages-to-the-benelux-countries_shoghi-effendi)), and say it is not *"a permissible way of life"* ([Messages to Canada](https://oceanlibrary.com/messages-to-canada_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_2684&selectionString=messagestocanada_v2_bahai_ocean_en-bl289.0~messagestocanada_v2_bahai_ocean_en-bl289.384)). One letter written on his behalf says that *"to let it find expression in sexual acts is wrong"* however fine the love, while acknowledging that being so afflicted *"is a great burden to a conscientious soul"* ([Messages from the Universal House of Justice: 1986-2001](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1986_2001)).

So the answer to "do Bahá'ís support LGBTQ people or not?" is that the texts call for respect, sympathy and open doors, with no prejudice or disdain, but they do not endorse same-sex relationships and they do not create advocacy structures. The stance is stated openly in the published Writings and House of Justice letters, though I found no welcome page of the kind other denominations post. In the library I also found nothing on legal or civil-rights advocacy as an institutional programme. Whether individual Bahá'ís support such causes as citizens is not addressed in these passages.

181upeh.question: What explanations do Bahá'í sources give for the claimed failed prophecies in 'Abdu'l-Bahá's Will and Testament, such as the Universal House of Justice not being established in Shoghi Effendi's lifetime and the succession
181upeh.draft:
The premise is worth examining first. Neither of your two examples is stated in the Will as an unconditional prediction. They are provisions, and the second is conditional in its own wording.

On the first point, the Will does not say the Universal House of Justice would be established in Shoghi Effendi's lifetime. It describes the institution and its relation to the Guardian: he is *"its sacred head and the distinguished member for life of that body"* ([The Universal House of Justice](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/the-universal-house-of-justice-research-department-of-20870#p22)). The Will leaves open when it would be elected, and the Guardian spent his ministry building the administrative order from which it would be elected. I found no text in the Will promising that it would exist by a given date.

On the second point, the succession of *"the first-born of his lineal descendants"* ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_1822&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1jg.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1jg.569)) is qualified in the same Will. The Guardian must appoint his successor in his own lifetime, and if the first-born does not manifest the needed spiritual qualities, the Guardian:

> "Thus, should the first-born of the Guardian of the Cause of God not manifest in himself the truth of the words: — ‘The child is the secret essence of its sire,’ that is, should he not inherit of the spiritual within him (the Guardian of the Cause of God) and his glorious lineage not be matched with a goodly character, then must he, (the Guardian of the Cause of God) choose another branch to succeed him."  
> — [The Will and Testament of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/the-will-and-testament-of-abdul-baha-20920#p17) So the text itself says the line might not continue through the first-born. It says nothing about what happens if no successor can be appointed at all. That is the situation the Universal House of Justice faced.

The House studied the texts, consulted the Hands of the Cause in the Holy Land, and concluded that there is *"no way to appoint or to legislate to make it possible to appoint a second Guardian to succeed Shoghi Effendi"* ([The Covenant](https://oceanlibrary.com/covenant_bahaullah/?paraId=para_127&selectionString=the_covenant_compilation_ocean_en-bl5v.0~the_covenant_compilation_ocean_en-bl5v.380)). It is a finding about the texts and the facts, not a claim that nothing unexpected happened.

On infallibility, the Guardian's guidance and the House's are separate. The House's guidance is conferred on the elected body: *"the body of the House of Justice is under the protection and unerring guidance of God"* ([Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_614&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_k1.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_k1.668)). The House also notes that *"nowhere is it stated that the infallibility of the Universal House of Justice is by virtue of the Guardian's membership or presence on that body"* ([The Universal House of Justice](https://oceanlibrary.com/universal-house-of-justice_bahaullah/?paraId=para_298&selectionString=universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.0~universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.1025)). The Guardian's absence therefore does not remove the House's guidance, and Shoghi Effendi himself wrote that the Guardianship does not *"detract from the powers granted to the Universal House of Justice"* ([The Universal House of Justice](https://oceanlibrary.com/universal-house-of-justice_bahaullah/?paraId=para_298&selectionString=universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.0~universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.1025)).

On why God would allow division, Bahá'u'lláh's words speak to the failure of attempts to put out God's light: *"the Hand of God is over your hands, that His Decree transcendeth all your devices"* ([Summons of the Lord of Hosts](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/summons-of-the-lord-of-hosts-bahaullah-20806#p467)). The Writings treat Covenant-breaking as the work of those who "rebelled" against the appointed centre ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_1823&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1hi.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1hi.1958)), not as a defect in the Covenant. The community's unity today runs through the elected House, which is the arrangement the Will itself provides for.

I have not searched for the historical account of the Hands' 1957 deliberations or the critics' arguments.
181upeh.reply:
A note on the sources first. P9 is a compilation passage by the Research Department of the Universal House of Justice. It is not a letter of the House, and it gives the Will's own words. I quote P2 first, since it is the core text, and keep P9 after it for the one point it adds.

The premise needs examining. Neither of your two examples is stated in the Will as an unconditional prediction. The Will makes provisions, and the succession provision is conditional in its own wording.

On succession, the Will says that after Shoghi Effendi *"will succeed the first-born of his lineal descendants"* ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_1822&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1jg.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1jg.569)). The same Will qualifies this. The Guardian must appoint his successor in his own lifetime, and if the first-born does not manifest the needed spiritual qualities, *"then must he, (the Guardian of the Cause of God) choose another branch to succeed him"* ([The Will and Testament of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/the-will-and-testament-of-abdul-baha-20920#p17)). So the text itself says the line might not pass to the first-born. It does not say what happens if no successor can be appointed at all. That is the situation the Universal House of Justice faced.

The House studied the texts, consulted the Hands of the Cause in the Holy Land, and found *"no way to appoint or to legislate to make it possible to appoint a second Guardian to succeed Shoghi Effendi"* ([The Covenant](https://oceanlibrary.com/covenant_bahaullah/?paraId=para_127&selectionString=the_covenant_compilation_ocean_en-bl5v.0~the_covenant_compilation_ocean_en-bl5v.380)). This is the House's finding about the texts and the facts, not a denial that the outcome was unexpected.

On the House of Justice, I found no sentence in the Will promising that it would be established in Shoghi Effendi's lifetime. The Will describes the institution and the Guardian's place in it. The compilation of the Will's words says the Guardian is *"its sacred head and the distinguished member for life of that body"* ([The Universal House of Justice](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/the-universal-house-of-justice-research-department-of-20870#p22)). That tells us how the two institutions relate, not when the House would be elected.

On infallibility, the guidance of the House rests on the elected body itself. 'Abdu'l-Bahá says *"the body of the House of Justice is under the protection and unerring guidance of God"* ([Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_614&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_k1.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_k1.668)). The House notes that *"nowhere is it stated that the infallibility of the Universal House of Justice is by virtue of the Guardian's membership or presence on that body"* ([The Universal House of Justice](https://oceanlibrary.com/universal-house-of-justice_bahaullah/?paraId=para_298&selectionString=universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.0~universal_house_of_justice_compilation_ocean_en-bl9m.1025)). The Guardian's absence therefore does not remove the House's guidance.

On why God would allow division, Bahá'u'lláh writes: *"Know ye not that the Hand of God is over your hands, that His Decree transcendeth all your devices"* ([Summons of the Lord of Hosts](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/summons-of-the-lord-of-hosts-bahaullah-20806#p467)). The Will treats those who rebel against the appointed centre as having departed from the Covenant ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_1823&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1hi.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl1hi.1958)). In the Writings the fault lies with the rebellion, not with the Covenant.

I have not searched for the historical account of the Hands' 1957 deliberations or for critics' arguments.

1dafwvt.question: Why is there so little representation of the Baha'i Faith in mainstream media despite its millions of adherents?
1dafwvt.draft:
The question assumes that the Faith's aim is visibility, so that a community of its size should show up in film, television and the news. The Writings start somewhere else. The Faith is young, it advances by teaching and service rather than publicity, and its Writings say plainly that its influence will be seen only over time.

'Abdu'l-Bahá compares it to the early Christians:



> "Grieve thou not over the slow advance of the Bahá'í Cause in that land. This is but the early dawn. Consider how, with the Cause of Christ, three hundred years had to go by, before its great influence was made manifest."  
> — [Selections from the Writings of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://oceanlibrary.com/selections-from-the-writings-of-abdul-baha/?paraId=para_271&selectionString=selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_b4.0~selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_b4.258)



Shoghi Effendi describes the present obscurity as a stage that precedes *"universal recognition"*:



> "If we all choose to tread faithfully His path, surely the day is not far distant when our beloved Cause will have emerged from the inevitable obscurity of a young and struggling Faith into the broad daylight of universal recognition."  
> — [Bahá’í Administration](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-administration_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_391&selectionString=baha_i_administration_selected_messages_1922_1932_3521e4ac6904cefdca84fce2627329c7-blcm.0~baha_i_administration_selected_messages_1922_1932_3521e4ac6904cefdca84fce2627329c7-blcm.431)



He also says we cannot yet judge what the Faith will contribute to society, including in the arts:



> "We have to wait only a few years to see how the spirit breathed by Bahá’u’lláh will find expression in the work of the artists. What you and some other Bahá’ís are attempting, are only faint rays that precede the effulgent light of a glorious morn. We cannot yet estimate the part the Cause is destined to play in the life of society. We have to give it time."  
> — [Uncompiled Published Letters](https://oceanlibrary.com/uncompiled-published-letters_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_3783&selectionString=published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl3jd.0~published_uncompiled_letters_from_shoghi_effendi_b2a6b4c2e078beaa6f19ad12bc5c92b39-bl3jd.72)



The Writings place the Faith's strength in lived example rather than public attention:



> "If we are true Bahá'ís speech is not needed. Our actions will help on the world, will spread civilization, will help the progress of science, and cause the arts to develop."  
> — [Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/bahai-sacred-writings-compilation-bahai-20777#p1269)



Teaching is to be done by *"the power of men's utterance"* ([Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh](https://oceanlibrary.com/gleanings-from-the-writings-of-bahaullah/?paraId=para_828&selectionString=gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_pq.0~gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_pq.717)) and with a *"kindly manner"*, not by pressing for attention. ([Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh](https://oceanlibrary.com/gleanings-from-the-writings-of-bahaullah/?paraId=para_828&selectionString=gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_pq.0~gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_pq.717)) A pilgrim's recollection of a talk, not a written text, adds that obscurity has also served as a protection for a young Faith, as it did for early Christianity. ([Pilgrimage in December](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/pilgrimage-in-december-john-and-valera-allen-12738#p75))

So the scarcity of mainstream depictions fits what the Writings describe for this stage. The work they point to is the quiet, local kind, and the arts are expected to flower later. People like Rainn Wilson who give the Faith a public voice are part of that gradual growth.
